Hi Samir — great talking yesterday. Per our conversation I attached a short 'implementation playbook' that walks through the model shortlisting logic we use during onboarding and the token/traffic worksheet you can fill out.

High-level ask before we run the capacity workshop tomorrow (30m):
- Confirm typical request/response sizes (avg user prompt length and expected model response length) for the three primary flows you mentioned (search-assist, summarization, and agent-reply). If you don't have exact numbers, ballpark ranges are fine.
- Indicate whether you need >8k context (long-form docs) or if 8k is sufficient.

What I'm sending in the playbook (TL;DR):
1) Model shortlist rationale (latency vs. cost vs. quality) with recommended defaults for web-scale QA and for long-context summarization.
2) Token profile worksheet (sample_token_profile.csv) where you'll list per-flow traffic & size percentiles.
3) Quick batch/cache knobs we typically suggest to reduce unit tokens without impacting latency.

If helpful, Dev will add a quick estimated QPS->GPU mapping during the call based on your traffic distribution.

Next steps: please drop the sample token profile back to me and we'll confirm the 30m workshop time.

Thanks — Ava

  * summarization: prompt 600 / 2,800 tokens, response 400 / 1,200 tokens (doc-level)

Thanks for the numbers, Samir — this is helpful. I ran a couple quick back-of-envelope calculations from the CSV snapshot you sent and the p95 sizes you provided. Notes below are purposely conservative.

Assumptions I used (conservative):
- Peak concurrent requesters: 3,200 users initiating at 0.02 QPS -> system QPS ~64
- Traffic distribution (peak): search-assist 55%, summarization 30%, agent-reply 15%
- Use p95 tokens for cost forecast; use median tokens for latency/throughput planning

Per-flow p95 tokens (request+response):
- search-assist: 120 + 220 = 340 tokens -> 55% of 64 QPS = 35 QPS -> ~11,900 tokens/s
- summarization (32k context): 2,800 + 1,200 = 4,000 tokens -> 30% of 64 QPS = 19 QPS -> ~76,000 tokens/s (this is the heavy one)
- agent-reply: 600 + 800 = 1,400 tokens -> 15% of 64 QPS = 10 QPS -> ~14,000 tokens/s

Aggregate peak token throughput: ~101,900 tokens/second. For a 60s sustained window that's ~6.1M tokens/min.

Operational implications and recommendations:
1) Model selection: for summarization we should test a high-context variant (32k) but with aggressive prefix KV caching and chunked document feeding. Candidate shortlist: Llama-3-32k (quantized), Redstone-32k (if available), and a mid-size 8k model baseline for search-assist.
2) Serving: summarization workload will dominate GPU memory & bandwidth. We recommend routing summarization requests to a dedicated pool optimized for long-context (larger per-request memory, fewer concurrent streams per GPU).
3) Batching: enable small micro-batches (2-4) for the summarization pool to improve GPU utilization; keep search-assist pool low-batch (1-2) to preserve latency.
4) Autoscaling: set scale-up threshold at sustained 70% GPU utilization measured over 30s; cooldown 90s. Pre-warm extra capacity for night/weekend spikes if you have region-specific peak patterns.

I'll prepare a quick capacity estimate mapping tokens/s to GPU counts for the workshop. If you can confirm region split (US/EU) and any compliance constraints for the summarization documents, I can finalize a recommended Dedicated pool sizing.

— Dev
